For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: Law-Invariant Operators for Stochastic Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.12361v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A central objective in stochastic mechanics is to separate deterministic physical behavior from the probability laws governing uncertain inputs. While classical spectral approaches achieve this separation in linear settings, nonlinear responses introduce interactions beyond conventional second-order variability response functions (VRF). Inspired by the spirit of VRFs, this work establishes that, for a fixed physical system, uncertainty propagation is described by a law-invariant operator mapping input realizations to responses, governed by the underlying physics and the deterministic parameters of the system. Different probability laws affect the input sampling and resulting response statistics, but not the mapping operator. We establish this law invariance under complete, invertible coordinate transformations and develop complementary, Fourier, fixed-reference polynomial-chaos (PCE) and finite element method (FEM) transfer formulations. Fourier captures nonlinear cross-frequency interactions and recovers the classical VRF in the appropriate linear limit, PCE describes coupling among stochastic modes, while FEM expresses the deterministic inverse-stiffness action. Neural approximations of these deterministic operators are investigated through analytical and finite-element benchmarks, examining cross-law generalization, the influence of training distributions and stochastic excitation, and the prediction of response fields and statistics. The results demonstrate the potential for reusing learned physical operators across different stochastic laws without retraining, while highlighting the importance of adequate training coverage and the challenges of accurately estimating low-probability events.
item.dc:creator: Vissarion Papadopoulos

item.title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
item.description: arXiv:2611.12424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions. We investigate whether physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations by incorporating governing equations and prescribed initial and boundary conditions. We introduce hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and its gradient-direction-aware extension (HO-PINN), which adjust the emphasis on physical constraints according to higher-priority losses. Hierarchical PINNs are compared with Vanilla PINN, tuned gradient boosting, support-vector regression, and Gaussian-process regression on a heat equation and three heterogeneous two-phase-flow benchmarks. Experiments use 20--1000 labelled states and ten paired seeds. Each label is one coordinate--state observation, not a complete simulation. At least one PINN variant achieves the highest mean primary-target \(R^2\) in each interpolation and equation-assisted forecasting comparison at 20 and 50 labels. The advantage for water saturation persists across all tested budgets. Hierarchical weighting reduces variability across runs in selected settings. These results demonstrate that known physics can support accurate neural surrogate predictions from very few solution observations, at substantially higher fitting cost than the tested classical regressors.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Katsuba, Oleg Rudenko, Egor Bugaev, Alexander Tarakanov

item.title: Efficient high-order Discontinuous Galerkin simulations of multi-species high-enthalpy flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.12511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Numerical simulation of hypersonic vehicles is an attractive approach to investigate the complex phenomena involved in such technologies. For this, second-order finite volume methods (FVM) are the established method in computational fluid dynamics, with the cost of high dissipation in affordable meshes, thus needing refined ones or adaptive mesh refinements techniques to obtain accurate results. An alternative is to make use of high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods, in particular discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM), once it achieves higher formal order of accuracy on element-local polynomial bases. Therefore the goal of this work is to present the numerical simulations of a two-dimensional scramjet configuration to test and verify the applicability of the DGSEM approach for a complex hypersonic flow where shock-shock interactions occur. Results revealed to be in agreement with reference FVM solvers, thus verifying the code implementation.
item.dc:creator: Beatriz Fag\'a, Georgii Oblapenko, Yiyang Zhu, Daniel Doehring, Manuel Torrilhon

item.title: Nonlinear integral equations for stress-controlled rheology: Collocation methods for Volterra equations with functional kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.12578v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a class of numerical collocation methods to solve a typical inverse problem that arises in the stress-controlled rheology of complex fluids with pronounced history-dependent response, where the relation between stress and flow rate is given by an integral constitutive equation as the material law. We demonstrate the method by calculating the creep response of a nontrivial model of a shear-thinning viscoelastic fluid where a stress overshoot in rate-controlled startup flow leads to ``sudden yielding'' in stress-controlled creep. Our method is able to address the long-time behavior of the model, distinguishing the amorphous solid from the stress-induced yielded fluid, and from the in-between case of infinite deformation that never achieves a stationary shear rate (proper creep). To this end, we implement a method with flexible time-stepping, and prove uniqueness of the solution and convergence of the methods for a broad class of highly viscoelastic non-linear rheological laws in integral form.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Domann, Thomas Voigtmann

item.title: On the entire solutions of Schr\"{o}der iteration functions of first and second kind
item.description: arXiv:2611.12593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S_{f,n}$ and $K_{f,n}$ denote Schr\"oder's methods of the first and second kind with given order $ n $ ($\geq 2 $) applied to an entire function $ f $. This article investigates the existence of the entire solutions $f$ whenever $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ are rational. Utilizing the Nevanlinna theory, we obtain the general form of entire solutions for such equations. It is proved that either of $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ is a non-identity rational map if and only if $f = p e^{q}$, for some polynomials $p$ and $q$. Additionally, we provide one recurrence relation of $K_{f,n}$ depending only upon $K_{f,n-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Subhasis Ghora, Gang Liu, Soumen Pal, Saminathan Ponnusamy

item.title: When is Polynomial Optimization SoS-Exact? Sufficient Regularization and Strict Gram Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Global minimization of multivariate polynomials is computationally difficult in general, and nonnegativity does not necessarily imply a sum-of-squares (SoS) representation. We show that adding sufficiently strong Euclidean regularization to a polynomial provides a general mechanism for overcoming such challenges. Namely, for any multivariate polynomial $P$ of degree at most $p$ with a nonzero linear coefficient, and any even integer $2d>p$, we prove that $m_\sigma(s)=P(s)+\frac{\sigma}{2d}\|s\|_2^{2d}$ is SoS exact for all sufficiently large $\sigma$. Furthermore, the shifted polynomial $m_\sigma-\min m_\sigma$ admits a positive-definite Gram representation on appropriately-shifted nonconstant monomials. Consequently, the global minimum and minimizer can be recovered exactly by a single degree-$d$ semidefinite programming (SDP) representation, whose size is polynomial in the dimension for fixed $d$, without requiring higher levels of the SoS hierarchy. The proof develops a degree-independent mechanism based on the Bregman remainder of the regularizer: its strict Gram margin absorbs the lower-degree polynomial perturbations. We further establish an analogous exact SDP regime for polynomial optimization over sufficiently small Euclidean balls, connecting large regularization with small-radius trust-region problems. Finally, we investigate how the algebraic structure of the regularizer governs the existence of a strict Gram margin, extending the mechanism beyond Euclidean norms while identifying limitations of coordinate-separable regularization.
item.dc:creator: Coralia Cartis, Wenqi Zhu

item.title: Convergence Analysis of an Upwind Finite-Difference Scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equations
item.description: arXiv:2301.06415v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the convergence of an upwind finite-difference scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations on a one-dimensional periodic domain, considering both the value function and the feedback control selected by the discrete pointwise minimization. For classical value functions whose time and spatial derivatives are H\"older continuous in their respective variables, we bound the error at the grid points by a constant times the sum of the time step and spatial mesh width each raised to their common H\"older exponent. This yields first-order convergence when these derivatives are Lipschitz continuous and the meshes are refined proportionally. Under additional spatial regularity of the problem data, we also prove convergence of both one-sided difference quotients of the discrete value function to the spatial derivative of the value function: the integral over space and time of the absolute error tends to zero for each difference quotient. We further establish convergence of the discrete controls to the continuous feedback control when the continuous pointwise minimizer is unique, regardless of how the discrete minimizers are selected. These theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the accuracy of the value-function approximation and the behavior of the computed feedback controls.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Inoue, Nao Hamamuki, Yuji Ito, Takahito Kashiwabara, Norikazu Saito, Hiroaki Yoshida

item.title: Data-proximal null-space networks for inverse problems
item.description: arXiv:2309.06573v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inverse problems with incomplete data are severely ill-posed and require regularization. Learned reconstructions incorporate prior information effectively, but their regularization properties are less well understood than those of classical variational methods. We propose data-proximal null-space networks, which post-process an initial reconstruction obtained by a classical regularization method and extend null-space networks by allowing learned corrections that are not restricted to the null space, while bounding their effect on the measured data by a prescribed tolerance. Combined with a convergent, possibly nonlinear regularization method, these networks yield convergent regularization methods with convergence rates and data-proximity bounds. A calmness-based analysis covers fixed networks with radial clipping even when the operator range is not closed; their correction outside the null space vanishes in the limit, so that they differ from null-space networks only at positive noise levels. For the limited-angle Radon transform, exact data consistency preserves the visible singularities of the initial reconstruction, whereas data proximity controls the visible error in a weak Sobolev norm proportional to the data norm, but not its singularities. For compactly supported objects, null-space networks act trivially, whereas data-proximal networks can still correct nearly invisible components. In limited-angle computed tomography, data-proximal networks substantially improve on null-space networks and, unlike residual networks, guarantee a prescribed bound on the data change.
item.dc:creator: J\"urgen Frikel, Simon G\"oppel, Markus Haltmeier

item.title: Finite element form-valued forms: Construction
item.description: arXiv:2503.03243v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a finite element discretization of $\ell$-form-valued $k$-forms on triangulation in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ for general $k$, $\ell$ and $n$ and any polynomial degree. The construction generalizes finite element Whitney forms for the de~Rham complex and their higher-order and distributional versions, the Regge finite elements and the Christiansen--Regge elasticity complex, the TDNNS element for symmetric stress tensors, the MCS element for traceless matrix fields, the Hellan--Herrmann--Johnson (HHJ) elements for biharmonic equations, and discrete divdiv and Hessian complexes in [Hu, Lin, and Zhang, 2025]. The construction discretizes the Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) diagrams. Applications of the construction include discretization of strain and stress tensors in continuum mechanics and metric and curvature tensors in differential geometry in any dimension.
item.dc:creator: Kaibo Hu, Ting Lin

item.title: Adaptive refinement in defeaturing problems via an equilibrated flux a posteriori error estimator
item.description: arXiv:2503.19784v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An adaptive refinement strategy, based on an equilibrated flux a posteriori error estimator, is proposed in the context of defeaturing problems. Defeaturing consists of removing features from complex domains to simplify mesh generation and reduce the computational cost of simulations. It is a common procedure, for example, in computer aided design for simulation-based manufacturing. However, depending on the problem at hand, geometrical simplification may significantly deteriorate the accuracy of the solution. The proposed adaptive strategy is hence twofold: starting from a defeatured geometry, it iteratively performs both standard mesh refinement and geometrical refinement by selecting, at each step, which features must be reintroduced to significantly improve accuracy. Similar adaptive strategies have been previously developed using residual-based error estimators within an IGA framework. Here, instead, we extend a previously developed equilibrated flux a posteriori error analysis, designed for standard finite element discretizations, to make it fully applicable within the adaptive procedure. In particular, we address the assembly of the equilibrated flux estimator in presence of elements trimmed by the boundary of included features, adopting an unfitted finite element strategy to handle feature inclusion. The resulting estimator allows us to bound both the defeaturing and the numerical sources of error, with additional contributions accounting for the weak imposition of boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Annalisa Buffa, Denise Grappein, Rafael V\'azquez

item.title: Spectral element methods for boundary-value problems of functional differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2507.20266v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove convergence of the spectral element method for piecewise polynomial collocation applied to periodic boundary value problems for functional differential equations. In particular, we prove that the numerical collocation solution approximates the true solution with accuracy of order $\mathrm{e}^{-\eta m}$ for some $\eta>0$ and increasing degree $m$ of the polynomials, provided that the true solution is analytical. This includes a case that is common in applications: differential equations where the right-hand side depends on a finite number of delayed arguments with parametric delays and real analytic coefficients. For state-dependent delays the spectral element method also converges under mild regularity assumptions, although analyticity of the solution cannot be trivially inferred from analyticity of the coefficients. In order to extend our convergence results to this case, we introduce the concept of extended local Lipschitz continuity of the right-hand side.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: And\`o, A., Sieber, J. Spectral element methods for boundary-value problems of functional differential equations. Bit Numer Math 66, 68 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Alessia And\`o, Jan Sieber

item.title: RJD-BASE: Multi-Modal Spectral Clustering via Randomized Joint Diagonalization
item.description: arXiv:2509.11981v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit the problem of spectral clustering in multimodal settings, where each data modality is encoded as a graph Laplacian. While classical approaches--including joint diagonalization, spectral co-regularization, and multiview clustering--attempt to align embeddings across modalities, they often rely on costly iterative refinement and may fail to directly target the spectral subspace relevant for clustering. In this work, we introduce two key innovations. First, we bring the power of randomization to this setting by sampling random convex combinations of Laplacians as a simple and scalable alternative to explicit eigenspace alignment. Second, we propose a principled selection rule based on Bottom-$k$ Aggregated Spectral Energy (BASE)--a $k$-dimensional extension of the directional smoothness objective from recent minimax formulations--which we uniquely apply as a selection mechanism rather than an optimization target. The result is Randomized Joint Diagonalization with BASE Selection (RJD-BASE), a method that is easily implementable, computationally efficient, aligned with the clustering objective, and grounded in decades of progress in standard eigensolvers. Through experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we show that RJD-BASE reliably selects high-quality embeddings, outperforming classical multimodal clustering methods at low computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Haoze He, Artemis Pados, Daniel Kressner

item.title: A posteriori existence for the Keller-Segel model via a finite volume - finite element scheme
item.description: arXiv:2509.17710v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive two forms of conditional a posteriori error estimates for a finite volume scheme approximating the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system. The estimates control the error in the $L^\infty(0,T, L^2(\Omega))$-norm and exhibit linear convergence in the mesh size, as observed in numerical experiments. Crucially, we show that, as long as the condition of the error estimate is satisfied, a weak solution exists. This means, as long as the numerical solution has good properties, we can rigorously infer existence of an exact solution.
item.dc:creator: Marc Hoffmann, Jan Giesselmann

item.title: A Low-Rank BUG Method for Sylvester-Type Equations
item.description: arXiv:2511.01735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a low-rank algorithm inspired by the Basis-Update and Galerkin (BUG) integrator to efficiently approximate solutions to Sylvester-type equations. The algorithm can exploit both the low-rank structure of the solution as well as any sparsity present to reduce computational complexity. In the worst case scenario, i.e. even when a standard dense solver, such as the Bartels-Stewart algorithm, is used for the reduced Sylvester equations generated by our approach, the overall computational complexity for constructing and solving the associated linear systems reduces to $\mathcal{O}\left(kr(n^2+m^2 +mn + r^2)\right)$, for $X\in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$, where $k$ is the number of iterations and $r$ the rank of the approximation, but any method can be used to exploit existing structure to optimize the solution even further.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Vretinaris

item.title: An L-Stable Sequential Implicit Two-Stage Fourth-Order Time Discretization with Second-Order Stiff Damping
item.description: arXiv:2512.01628v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a fully implicit, sequential two-stage time discretization for stiff systems using physical quantities and their rates of change. Coefficients are determined by direct Taylor matching, and convergence analysis proves fourth-order accuracy at both midpoint and endpoint for fixed smooth systems. Pole and imaginary-axis boundary analysis, together with the maximum modulus principle, characterizes the \(L\)-stable family. Within this family, \(C_q=5/183\) uniquely cancels the leading inverse-power term and gives the full-step amplification factor quadratic stiff decay, while \(C_a=\frac{25-\sqrt{105}}{780}\) yields the highest accuracy. The method combines \(L\)-stability with second-order stiff damping, two-stage fourth-order accuracy, and sequential implicitness. In contrast, fourth-order Gauss--Legendre and symmetric Hermite--Obreshkov schemes are \(A\)-stable rather than \(L\)-stable; their variants must sacrifice per-stage accuracy to improve stiff stability. Among \(L\)-stable methods, two-stage Radau IIA and TR--BDF2 have third- and second-order accuracy, respectively, while SDIRK requires five stages for fourth order. Gauss and Radau stages must be solved in a coupled manner. Stiff ODE and scalar tests verify fourth-order convergence and quadratic stiff decay. Finite-volume tests show fourth-order joint convergence on smooth one-dimensional problems and fast-mode damping in two-dimensional cases. At the same acoustic error threshold, the method uses eight implicit stages, whereas three-stage Radau IIA uses twelve. Finally, the sequential formulation keeps each Newton system at the state dimension, reducing its size, improving efficiency, and facilitating parallel computation.
item.dc:creator: Zhixin Huo

item.title: Singular spaces for computing the structured distance to singularity
item.description: arXiv:2603.01233v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finding the distance to singularity for a matrix is a ubiquitous problem in numerical linear algebra, and is elegantly solved by the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem. Its structured variant arises when one considers structured matrices and wants to preserve their structure. This problem is important for several matrix nearness problems that either entirely or partly reduce to a structured distance to singularity problem. In this work, we propose a new method for the structured distance to singularity problem based on singular spaces, that is, linear subspaces consisting of singular matrices. We study the properties of these spaces to guide the construction of the algorithm. In the Tikhonov regularized formulation, the method globally minimizes a certain objective function alternately in its arguments. We show that a restricted family of singular spaces suffices to attain the best possible improvement in a single iteration. In many of the numerical comparisons, the proposed method yields substantial reductions in running time when compared with existing methods, while the computed distances to singularity remain comparable. These gains allow larger problems to be solved within practical running times.
item.dc:creator: Lauri Nyman

item.title: Splitting-strategies for arbitrary-order fully mixed finite element discretizations of the Biot equations
item.description: arXiv:2603.18241v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the fully-mixed formulation of the Biot equations which is characterized by a symmetric coupling between flow and deformation while each subphysics has internally a saddle point structure. This enables the use of stable mixed finite elements for each subproblem without a strong compatibility condition across the two subphysics. To exploit this flexibility while preserving the conservation structure of both subproblems, we consider fully mixed finite element methods in which the symmetry of the elastic stress tensor is enforced weakly, often referred to as a five-field formulation. The resulting mixed formulation exhibits an overarching saddle-point structure whose stability is determined by suitable inf-sup conditions. Inf-sup stability is established for several families of discrete spaces of arbitrary order, leading to optimal a priori error estimates. Iterative splitting strategies following the classical fixed-stress split with additional tuning are specifically investigated for the fully mixed formulation with proof of convergence and rates depending on the coupling strength. Contrary to previous analyses on coupled problems with a symmetric structure, we theoretically prove the efficacy of negative stabilization, consistent with Schur-complement ideas. Numerical results based on analytical solutions and the classical 2D Mandel problem and a 3D footing problem are presented supporting the theory.
item.dc:creator: Fleurianne Bertrand, Jakub Wiktor Both, Tugay Da\u{g}l{\i}

item.title: Admissible Lax-Wendroff Flux Reconstruction Method with Automatic Differentiation on Adaptive Curved Meshes for Relativistic Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.20608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The relativistic hydrodynamics (RHD) equations can give rise to solutions which have shocks, contact discontinuities, and other sharp structures, which interact and evolve over time. Capturing these sharp waves effectively requires a mesh with high resolution, making the scheme computationally expensive. In this work, adaptive mesh refinement is used with the high-order Lax-Wendroff flux reconstruction (LWFR) method to solve the system of RHD equations, which is closed with general Synge-type equations of state. To make the scheme Jacobian-free, the idea of automatic differentiation is incorporated for computing the temporal derivatives in the time average flux approximations. The high-order method is blended with an admissible low-order method at the subcell level to control the Gibbs oscillations and maintain the physical admissibility of the solution. Finally, several test cases involving high Lorentz factors, low densities, low pressures, strong shock waves, and other discontinuities are used to demonstrate the robustness, accuracy, and effectiveness of the proposed method. These simulations are performed with AMR using various linear and curved meshes to show the scheme's efficiency and ability to handle complex geometries.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Basak, Arpit Babbar, Harish Kumar, Praveen Chandrashekar

item.title: Fast and Stable Gradient Approximation for Quadratic Forms of Hermitian Matrix Functions
item.description: arXiv:2605.12801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Objectives involving quadratic forms $u^*f(A(\theta))u$ for Hermitian $A$ arise widely in scientific computing and machine learning. Lanczos efficiently approximates these quantities, but differentiating through its recurrence can introduce numerical instability and costly reorthogonalization. Building on existing low-rank Krylov approximations of Fr\'echet derivatives, we develop a matrix-free gradient implementation that reuses the forward Lanczos quantities without differentiating through the recurrence. We analyze its discrepancy from the exact gradient of the finite Lanczos approximation, deriving an exact residual-coupled error identity and a bound involving the best degree-$(m-1)$ uniform polynomial approximation error of $f'$, multiplied by a basis-sensitivity factor. The discrepancy vanishes when the Krylov subspace is invariant. Experiments demonstrate accurate gradients and runtime improvements over differentiated-Lanczos and modified-Arnoldi baselines. It remains numerically stable without reorthogonalization in all tested settings, including cases where adjoint-based Lanczos differentiation becomes unstable.
item.dc:creator: Navjot Singh, Kipton Barros, Xiaoye Sherry Li

item.title: Comparing algebraic cubature rules on spline curved elements
item.description: arXiv:2607.10485v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compare four methods for the construction of algebraic cubature rules on planar elements, whose boundary is tracked by splines. The methods, that we have developed over the last two decades, are based on Green theorem together with some cornerstones of polynomial approximation theory: Gaussian quadrature,Tchakaloff theorem, discretized Chebyshev expansion (hyperinterpolation), Fekete-like interpolation. We discuss their advantages and drawbacks in view of the application to curved polytopal element methods. We have also made freely available at a single site the corresponding open-source Matlab codes.
item.dc:creator: A. Sommariva, M. Vianello

item.title: Strong error bounds at low regularity for a time approximation of the stochastic KdV equation driven by small additive noise
item.description: arXiv:2607.14813v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study strong temporal approximation of periodic stochastic Korteweg--de Vries equation driven by small additive \(Q\)-Wiener noise of amplitude \(\mathcal O(\varepsilon)\), \(0<\varepsilon\ll1\) under $H^s$-regularity, $s=1,2$. This is a challenging problem, due to the additional derivative term in the nonlinearity and the lack of suitable exponential moment bounds for the exact solutions. Exploiting the small-noise regime, we first decompose the solution into a deterministic KdV flow and a stochastic component; then we linearize the obtained stochastic equation and approximate the resulting equation by means of Fourier analytic techniques. Combining the small-noise linearization error, the discretization error of the linearized equation, and the deterministic temporal approximation error, and assuming suitable conditions on the deterministic solver, we get strong errors of size $\mathcal{O}(\tau+\varepsilon^2)$ under \(H^1\)-regularity and of size $\mathcal{O}(\tau^2+\varepsilon^2)$ under $H^2$-regularity. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first strong error bounds achieved for numerical time approximations of the stochastic KdV at low regularity.
item.dc:creator: Jianbo Cui, Raffaele D'Ambrosio, Stefano Di Giovacchino, Liying Sun

item.title: Self-similar structure of non-isothermal variable-density mushy Stefan problems and an improved low-Mach enthalpy method
item.description: arXiv:2608.00960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The enthalpy method was introduced in the late 1970s to simulate phase-change problems on fixed grids without explicitly tracking the moving phase-change front. It remains one of the most widely used approaches in academic and commercial software for the simulation of industrial melting and solidification processes. For pure phase-change materials (PCMs) that melt or solidify at a single temperature, the enthalpy method introduces an artificial mushy region bounded by the solidus temperature, $T^{\rm sol}$, and the liquidus temperature, $T^{\rm liq}$. As the numerical parameter $\Delta T=T^{\rm liq}- T^{\rm sol}$ approaches zero, the solution obtained with the enthalpy method is generally assumed to converge to that of the classical Stefan problem, in which the phase-change front is infinitesimally thin. This assumption is largely based on benchmark studies performed under the simplifying assumption of equal solid and liquid densities. In this work, we systematically investigate the accuracy and spatio-temporal convergence properties of the enthalpy method for both low- and high-density-ratio phase-change problems. Because the limiting behavior $\Delta T\rightarrow0$ is difficult to realize numerically, owing to the diminishing thickness of the mushy region, we formulate and analyze the finite-$\Delta T$ mushy Stefan problem solved by the enthalpy method. We show that this problem possesses a self-similar structure that reduces the governing equations to a boundary-value problem involving two unknown parameters. The theoretical analysis also enables improvements to our previously developed low-Mach enthalpy method, enhancing its stability and accuracy as the density ratio between the two phases increases from $\mathcal{O}(1)$ to $\mathcal{O}(3)$.
item.dc:creator: Yavkreet Swami, Amneet Pal Singh Bhalla

item.title: Quadratic Stiff Damping and Full-Step Asymptotic Preservation in a Two-Stage Fourth-Order Finite-Volume Method for Cattaneo Relaxation
item.description: arXiv:2608.03256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We couple a previously analyzed L-stable sequential two-stage fourth-order time formula to a specified fifth-order finite-volume residual for the periodic Goldstein--Taylor/Cattaneo equation in one and two dimensions. The required second time derivative is chosen as the exact derivative along the semi-discrete trajectory, $\mathcal G_h(U)=D\mathcal L_h(U)\mathcal L_h(U)$. For our linear reconstruction and flux, applying the same conservative face operator to $V=\mathcal L_h(U)$ yields this derivative exactly. A central face flux produces a skew-adjoint divergence--gradient pair, allowing a fixed-grid full-step asymptotic-preserving (AP) theorem for the implemented operator; for the specified central-flux discrete heat target, a wave-speed Rusanov flux has the same derivative closure but fails that target. This statement is not a claim about Rusanov-type discretizations in general. Within the previously established L-stable parameter interval, $C_q=5/183$ is the unique fixed coefficient within the admissible family, in the sense of the asymptotic damping exponent, that cancels the leading inverse-stiffness amplification, giving $R(-x)=O(x^{-2})$ rather than the generic $O(x^{-1})$ as $x=\Delta t/\delta\to\infty$. Independent high-precision scalar calculations and the actual two-dimensional finite-volume transverse mode verify the exponent up to $x=10^5$; a mixed slow--fast state shows the resulting flux-error advantage for specified data. This damping statement does not optimize finite-stiffness accuracy or computational efficiency. The AP statements below concern the fixed-grid linear periodic problem with exact stage solutions; no mesh-uniform or nonlinear AP result is claimed.
item.dc:creator: Zhixin Huo, Yangnan Su

item.title: Robust High-Order Projector-Splitting Integrators
item.description: arXiv:2608.17157v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop and analyze an increment-based $K$-$L$ integrator for dynamical low-rank approximation. This formulation eliminates the separate backward $S$-step and is algebraically equivalent to the fixed-increment projector-splitting integrator of Lubich and Oseledets. We establish a relaxed-exactness estimate that bounds the error in the low-rank approximation in terms of the prescribed increment error, with constants independent of small singular values. This estimate provides a framework for achieving robust high-order convergence through sufficiently accurate increments. We then construct low-rank Runge--Kutta methods in which both the stage and final approximations are computed using the $K$-$L$ integrator, without basis augmentation or rank truncation. Since classical Runge--Kutta order conditions alone do not guarantee robust high-order convergence for this construction, we derive sufficient conditions on the coefficients that ensure the required stage accuracy and establish robust convergence of order $p$. We identify explicit Runge--Kutta schemes of orders $p=2,3,4$ satisfying these conditions, and numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Shiheng Zhang, Jingwei Hu

item.title: Minimax-Optimal Early Stopping for SGD via the Discrepancy Principle
item.description: arXiv:2609.11273v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study early stopping for stochastic gradient descent with a constant step size applied to noisy linear inverse problems with polynomially decaying spectrum. The iteration is stopped by the discrepancy principle, that is, as soon as its residual reaches the prescribed noise level. For H\"older source conditions below a saturation level determined by the polynomial decay, we prove that the mean-square reconstruction error at the stopping index is bounded by the classical rate, up to an explicit factor involving the step size and the incoherence of the design, and that the expected number of iterations is of the order of the oracle stopping index. The rate is minimax-optimal for deterministic noise whenever the spectrum contains an eigenvalue at the oracle scale and this factor stays bounded. The step size is restricted by a spectrum-weighted incoherence condition. The analysis allows rank-deficient designs and inconsistent observations.
item.dc:creator: Tim Jahn, Loucas Pillaud-Vivien, Adrien Schertzer

item.title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03263v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. This results in excessive diffusion of vorticity and is one of the main reasons for the physical inaccuracy of the algorithm. We propose Kernelized Stable Fluids with Sparse Cholesky Preconditioning (KSF-Chol) in order to address this shortcoming and make the algorithm thereby suitable for engineering problems and scientific computing. The algorithm is modified by replacing the linear interpolation approach with kernel interpolation in the advection step. We accelerate the computationally expensive kernel interpolation by using sparse Cholesky preconditioning and a near-/far-field approach and optimize both methods for computations on a uniform Cartesian grid. KSF-Chol achieves per time step a near-linear computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N\log^d(N/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{chol}}))$ in space and time. We test KSF-Chol against reference solvers and numerical reference data on multiple 2D and 3D benchmarks and demonstrate a significantly reduced numerical diffusion as well as a competitive accuracy concerning the computation of relevant flow quantities.
item.dc:creator: Lennart Scholz, Aras Bacho, Houman Owhadi

item.title: A weak Galerkin finite element method for the coupled Stokes-Biot problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper,we consider a stable numerical method for the Stokes-Biot model. We adopt the standard formulation of the Stokes equations coupled with the mixed formulation of the Biot system involving the additional total pressure variable. We construct the semi-discrete scheme on polygonal meshes by employing weak Galerkin finite element methods for spatial discretization. It is convenient to incorporate the interface conditions into the semi-discrete scheme via the edge-based degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we give a fully discrete scheme based on the backward Euler method. We establish the well-posedness of these two schemes and provide a rigorous error analysis. Finally, we present some numerical examples to verify the convergence and stability of our algorithm under a wide range of some physical parameters.
item.dc:creator: Rui Li, Hui Peng, Xiuli Wang

item.title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.07360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models under gravitational force, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.
item.dc:creator: K. Sudarshan Kumar, Boniface Nkonga, Praveen Chandrashekar

item.title: Mathematical analysis and vectorized FEM implementation of logarithmic strain space framework for finite strains: a case study on elastoplasticity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the mathematical and computational aspects of the logarithmic strain space framework for finite-strain models in nonlinear continuum mechanics, focusing on the classical von Mises elastoplastic model with linear kinematic hardening. To overcome the lack of coercivity and lower-semicontinuity in the quadratic Hencky energy, we introduce higher-gradient regularization and prove the existence of energetic solutions for rate-independent quasistatic evolution under time-dependent Dirichlet loading. Complementarily, we develop a vectorized MATLAB finite-element implementation of the framework leveraging page-wise matrix functions and operations, and our custom vectorization library. Computational benchmarks show that local tensor operations are significantly accelerated, the logarithmic-strain approach does not substantially increase computational costs, and the implementation robustly handles large rotations and deformations.
item.dc:creator: Miroslav Frost, Martin Kru\v{z}\'ik, Alexej Moskovka, Jan Valdman

item.title: Finite-time Cholesky Factorization
item.description: arXiv:2611.09706v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an algorithm for estimating the Cholesky factorization of positive, semi-definite matrices without pivoting. Our method has the same data access pattern as the canonical Cholesky method, and therefore is amenable to familiar hardware optimization techniques. Our method interprets the factorization task as a variational problem and in turn solves it using an induced dynamical system. We study the rate of convergence of this dynamical system to its stationary state for both positive definite and semi-definite matrices. Numerical experiments validate that our method is competitive with pivoted Cholesky on several practical examples.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Manavalan, Carola Bibiane Schoenlieb

item.title: Exploring specialization and sensitivity of convolutional neural networks under simultaneous image augmentations
item.description: arXiv:2503.03283v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Drawing parallels with the way biological networks are studied, the authors adapt the treatment--control paradigm to explainable artificial intelligence research and enrich it through multi-parametric input alterations. A framework for investigating internal inference impacted by input data augmentations is proposed to address the real-world scenario with multiple simultaneously applied treatments instead of observing a single effect. The internal changes in network operation are reflected in activation changes measured by variance, which can be decomposed into components related to each augmentation by employing Sobol indices and Shapley values. To facilitate distinguishing model-related specifics from the self-interactions of augmentations, an auxiliary variable responsible for their permutations has been incorporated into the analysis. The resulting quantities enable one to visualize sensitivity to different variables and use them as features for further analysis and processing, including guided masking of activations. In addition, a method for single-class sensitivity analysis is introduced through a pipeline that involves class selection according to their match with the prediction bias generated by targeted damaging of the activations. Three convolutional networks, namely AlexNet, VGG11, and ResNet18, have been evaluated via the designed framework, with two vision transformers, ViT-b-16 and Swin-t, partially complementing the findings. Two sets of augmentations, consisting of five and seven distinct input transformations applied simultaneously, have been utilized as sources of variance in the image domain. Relying on the observed parallels, the authors assume that the developed framework can potentially be transferred to the study of biological neural networks in complex environments, as well as enhance the design of autonomous decision-making systems.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Kharyuk, Sergey Matveev, Ivan Oseledets

item.title: Variable Projected Augmented Lagrangian Methods for Generalized Lasso Problems
item.description: arXiv:2510.24140v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce variable projected augmented Lagrangian (VPAL) methods for solving generalized nonlinear Lasso problems with improved speed and accuracy. By eliminating the nonsmooth variable via soft-thresholding, VPAL transforms the problem into a smooth reduced formulation. We develop a preconditioned variant based on curvature-informed updates and investigate its performance for both linear and nonlinear inverse problems. We prove convergence guarantees for both standard and preconditioned VPAL under mild assumptions and show that variable projection leads to faster convergence and higher solution quality. The method seamlessly extends to nonlinear inverse problems, where it outperforms traditional approaches in applications such as phase retrieval and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging. Across linear and nonlinear imaging applications, numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed methods, highlighting the potential of variable projection for large-scale inverse problems.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Aleotti, Davide Bianchi, Florian Bossmann, Riley Yizhou Chen, Matthias Chung

item.title: A Benamou-Brenier Proximal Splitting Method for Constrained Unbalanced Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2512.09250v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The dynamic formulation of optimal transport, also known as the Benamou-Brenier formulation, has been extended to the unbalanced case by introducing a source term in the continuity equation. When this source term is penalized based on the Fisher-Rao metric, the resulting model is referred to as the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) setting, and allows for the comparison between any two positive measures without the need for equalized total mass. In recent work, we introduced a constrained variant of this model, in which affine integral equality constraints are imposed along the measure path. In the present paper, we propose a further generalization of this framework, which allows for constraints that apply not just to the density path but also to the momentum and source terms, and incorporates affine inequalities in addition to equality constraints. We prove, under suitable assumptions on the constraints, the well-posedness of the resulting class of convex variational problems. The paper is then primarily devoted to developing an effective numerical pipeline that tackles the corresponding constrained optimization problem based on finite difference discretizations and parallel proximal schemes. Our proposed framework encompasses standard balanced and unbalanced optimal transport, as well as a multitude of natural and practically relevant constraints, and we highlight its versatility via several synthetic and real data examples.
item.dc:creator: Mao Nishino, Martin Bauer, Tom Needham, Nicolas Charon

item.title: All-Pass Function OPF: A Solver-Friendly, Physics-Preserving Approximation of AC OPF
item.description: arXiv:2601.14468v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper presents a rational approximation of the AC optimal power flow (AC OPF) problem based on an all-pass approximation of the exponential power flow kernel. The classical AC OPF relies on trigonometric coupling between bus voltage phasors, which yields a nonconvex program with oscillatory derivatives that can slow, or in some cases destabilize, interior-point methods. We replace the trigonometric terms with an all-pass function (APF) approximation whose real and imaginary components act as smooth surrogates for the cosine and sine functions, and we introduce a pre-rotation to shift the argument of the approximation toward its most accurate region, ensuring that the reformulated power flow model preserves physical loss behavior, maintains the symmetry of the classical kernels, and improves the conditioning of the Jacobian and Hessian matrices. The proposed APF OPF formulation remains nonconvex, as in the classical model, but it eliminates trigonometric evaluations and empirically produces larger and more stable Newton steps under standard interior-point solvers. Numerical results on more than 25 IEEE and PGLib test systems ranging from 9 to 10{,}000 buses demonstrate that the APF OPF model achieves solutions with accuracy comparable to that of the classical formulation while reducing solver times, indicating a more solver-friendly nonconvex representation of AC OPF. All code, functions, verification scripts, and generated results are publicly available on \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/APF-OPF}{GitHub}, along with a README describing how to run and reproduce the experiments.
item.dc:creator: Milad Hasanzadeh, Amin Kargarian, Javad Lavaei

item.title: Persistent-Transient Policy Evaluation for Markov Chains via Minimal Peripheral Quotients
item.description: arXiv:2602.00474v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study fixed-policy evaluation for finite Markov chains that may be reducible and periodic. Classical evaluation methods with gain and bias decomposition are not always diagnostic: the gain records only invariant Ces\`aro averages, while persistent phase-dependent behavior is absorbed into the bias together with genuinely transient effects. We identify the real peripheral invariant subspace $\mathcal{K}(P)$ of the transition matrix $P$ as the source of this ambiguity. Quotienting by $\mathcal{K}(P)$ is the minimal exact quotient that removes all non-decaying modes and makes the remaining dynamics strictly stable. After choosing a gauge projection $\Pi$ with kernel $\mathcal{K}(P)$, the reward admits a unique decomposition $r = g_\Pi^\star + (I-P)v_\Pi^\star$, where $g_\Pi^\star$ is a persistent regime profile and $v_\Pi^\star$ is a gauge-fixed transient component. An exact comparison with classical normalized gain and bias shows that the new pair reallocates the same information into a persistent profile and a gauge-fixed representative of the transient quotient. This decomposition reconstructs finite-horizon returns, recovers statewise average reward, admits a transient-cost interpretation, and yields a stable estimator under a generative model.
item.dc:creator: Yang Xu, Vaneet Aggarwal

item.title: Closed-Form Implicit Neural Representations
item.description: arXiv:2602.07603v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Training implicit neural representations (INRs) to capture fine-scale details typically relies on iterative backpropagation and is often hindered by spectral bias when the target exhibits highly non-uniform frequency content. We propose ELM-INR, a backpropagation-free INR that decomposes the domain into overlapping subdomains and fits each local problem using an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) in closed form, replacing iterative optimization with stable linear least-squares solutions. This design yields fast and numerically robust reconstruction by combining local predictors through a partition of unity. To understand where approximation becomes difficult under fixed local capacity, we analyze the method from a spectral Barron norm perspective, which reveals that global reconstruction error is dominated by regions with high spectral complexity. Building on this insight, we introduce BEAM, an adaptive mesh refinement strategy that balances spectral complexity across subdomains to improve reconstruction quality in capacity-constrained regimes.
item.dc:creator: Woojin Cho, Junghwan Park

item.title: Active Learning for Conditional Generative Compressed Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2605.05435v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative compressed sensing uses the range of a pretrained generator as a nonlinear model for recovering structured signals from limited measurements. We study a conditional version of this problem for image recovery from subsampled Fourier measurements using prompt-conditioned generative models. Our framework separates two roles of conditioning: the prompt used to design the sampling distribution and the prompt used to define the recovery model. For ReLU and Lipschitz conditional generators, we prove stable recovery bounds showing that prompt-matched Christoffel sampling retains the same Christoffel complexity constant as existing near-optimal generative compressed sensing theory, while prompt mismatch incurs an explicit compatibility penalty. Experiments with Stable Diffusion show that prompts meaningfully reshape Christoffel sampling distributions and influence image recovery. Overall, our results suggest treating prompts as design variables for sensing, approximation, and recovery, opening new directions for the practical use of conditional generative models in compressed sensing, where conditioning, sampling, and optimization must be considered jointly.
item.dc:creator: Alexander DeLise, Nick Dexter

item.title: INEUS: Iterative Neural Solver for High-Dimensional PIDEs
item.description: arXiv:2605.06281v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce INEUS, a meshfree iterative neural solver for partial integro-differential equations (PIDEs). The method replaces the explicit evaluation of nonlocal jump integrals with single-jump sampling and reformulates PIDE solving as a sequence of recursive regression problems. Like Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), INEUS learns global solutions over the entire space-time domain, yet it offers a more efficient treatment of nonlocal terms and avoids the computationally expensive differentiation of full PIDE residuals. These features make INEUS particularly well suited for high-dimensional PDEs and PIDEs. Supported by a contraction-based convergence proof for linear PIDEs, our numerical experiments show that INEUS delivers accurate and scalable solutions for various high-dimensional linear and nonlinear examples.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Loup Dupret, Davide Gallon, Patrick Cheridito

item.title: Breakeven complexity: A new perspective on neural partial differential equation solvers
item.description: arXiv:2605.15399v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural surrogate solvers of partial differential equations (PDEs) promise dramatic speedups over numerical methods, especially in scenarios requiring many solves. However, current accuracy-based evaluations do not fully consider two central issues: (1) neural solvers incur substantial up-front costs for data generation, training, and tuning; and (2) classical solvers can also generate low-fidelity solutions at a sufficiently low simulation cost. To explicitly account for these realities and fully incorporate end-to-end costs, we propose an evaluation framework centered on breakeven complexity, a metric that counts the forward solves before a learned solver is cost-effective relative to an error-equivalent traditional solver. To evaluate this measure, we apply scaling laws to determine how much training budget to allocate to data generation and discuss how to achieve smooth error-matching in diverse settings. We evaluate the breakeven complexity of multiple neural PDE solvers on three PDEs on 2D periodic domains from APEBench and a novel benchmark of flows past multiple obstacles generated by the GPU-native PyFR code. Among other findings, our results suggest that neural PDE solvers become more effective as problems get harder in terms of cost, dimension, rollout, physics regime (e.g. higher Reynolds number), etc.
item.dc:creator: Yijing Zhang, Nicholas Roberts, Tanya Marwah, Mikhail Khodak

item.title: A stochastic gradient algorithm for non-separable optimization with convergence guarantee
item.description: arXiv:2606.10383v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study smooth parameterized non-separable objectives of the form $\mathcal L(\theta)=F(Y(\theta))$, where a global operator couples the outputs of all training samples. We analyze two stochastic gradient constructions within this output-space framework: the ideal per-batch gradient $G$, obtained by row sampling of the full output gradient, and a cached surrogate $H$ for parameterized updates in which full-data quantities are expensive to evaluate. For uniformly sampled batches, the ideal estimator has a deterministic batch-size scaling and a second moment controlled by the full output gradient. Using this structure, we establish local high-probability confinement and convergence for fixed positive step sizes on a prescribed parameter neighborhood under a power-type gradient inequality, with linear and polynomial regimes determined by its exponent. For the cached surrogate, a Lyapunov function couples the objective gap with the cache error and yields analogous local results on the corresponding non-exit event. The theory includes explicit path-length, confinement, and rate bounds; numerical experiments illustrate finite-budget decay trends and the effects of global output-gradient sampling, batch restriction, and cache tracking.
item.dc:creator: Yingzhou Li, Ruofan Wu

item.title: Improved Scaling for Fast Mode of Ozaki Scheme II
item.description: arXiv:2606.29129v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ozaki scheme II emulates high-precision matrix multiplication using low-precision integer matrix operations based on the Chinese remainder theorem (CRT). It first scales the high-precision matrices to convert them into integer matrices. For this scaling step, Ozaki scheme II provides two modes: accurate mode, which uses INT8 matrix multiplication to estimate scaling factors, and fast mode, which applies the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality at lower computational cost. We show that the existing formula lacks scale invariance; multiplying the input matrices by a constant changes the effective bit width of the integer matrices in the scaling step, causing accuracy degradation or CRT recovery failure. To address this, we propose a revised scaling formula derived from the CRT uniqueness condition via the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. The proposed formula is scale-invariant by construction, guarantees that the CRT uniqueness condition is always satisfied, and introduces no additional overhead over the original fast mode. Experiments on an NVIDIA GH200 GPU show that the proposed method achieves accuracy comparable to that of accurate mode while maintaining throughput comparable to that of fast mode. In the accuracy--throughput trade-off, the proposed method overcomes the accuracy limitation of fast mode and the throughput constraint of accurate mode, offering a superior accuracy and performance.
item.dc:creator: Shota Kawakami, Daisuke Takahashi

item.title: Investigation of the Asymptotic Properties of Active Impedance in Large Finite Array Antennas
item.description: arXiv:2608.17844v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper presents an improved full-wave solver for finite array antennas, and uses this solver to examine asymptotic properties of active impedance for large regular arrays. The improved solver is based on a preconditioning scheme that has been adapted for use on more general finite geometries, and an improved data structure. These two improvements result in a fast and stable solver with a lower memory footprint. By investigating the active impedance of the center element in finite arrays it is found that, even for arrays with 1000 elements, asymptotic behavior may differ appreciably from infinite arrays. Tied to these properties, different predictors on how the active impedance of the center element in the array behaves are presented. The two best predictors work very well for the wideband arrays investigated, and may be used to decide when array approximations, such as unit cell methods, are appropriate, rather than general statements on array size.
item.dc:creator: Harald Hultin, Lucas {\AA}kerstedt, B. L. G. Jonsson

item.title: Accelerated primal-dual dynamical systems for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
item.description: arXiv:2609.01415v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose accelerated inertial primal-dual dynamics for convex optimization problems with nonlinear convex inequality constraints. The proposed dynamics combine Nesterov accelerated vanishing damping $\alpha/t$, a projected augmented-Lagrangian multiplier, and tangent extrapolation of the constraint mapping. Without assuming strong convexity, we establish global well-posedness and simultaneous $\mathcal O(t^{-2})$ decay rates for the constraint violation and the objective residual when $\alpha\geq3$ and the extrapolation parameter satisfies a suitable compatibility condition. Under stricter parameter conditions, with $\alpha>3$, we further prove that the primal-dual trajectory converges to a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker pair, both residuals decay as $o(t^{-2})$. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Xin He

item.title: Holomorphic Cauchy Networks for Efficient Stationary Tail Computation in High-Dimensional Reflected Brownian Motions
item.description: arXiv:2610.36558v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stationary tail computation for high-dimensional reflected Brownian motions (RBMs) remains computationally challenging. Building on NN4MGF's shared-coordinate basic-adjoint-relationship (BAR) framework, we develop Holomorphic Cauchy Networks (HCNs). Native complex-valued rational Cauchy subnetworks enforce holomorphicity on pole-free domains, removing sampled Cauchy-Riemann penalties and their input-derivative graphs. Exact origin anchoring and boundary-coordinate exclusion enforce structural identities, while anchored interactions represent dependent transforms. Under holomorphic-log assumptions, we establish simultaneous value and first-derivative approximation for the constrained architectures and a mixed-derivative lower bound for coordinate-only representations under nonzero cross-covariance. Closed-form real-axis derivatives and sequential backpropagation further control memory. On the same NVIDIA H100 NVL, the tested 30D HCN configuration uses approximately tenfold less peak allocated memory and has 9.7-fold lower mean update time than NN4MGF; extrapolation to the respective scheduled update counts gives a projected full-schedule update-time ratio of 58.2. With 64 million sampled base inputs per high-dimensional run, HCN reaches 50 dimensions on a laptop GPU with 6.367% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8. Degree-matched comparisons yield lower reported mean relative errors over the primary evaluation ranges, including 1.422% versus 6.684% on the 2D Harrison non-product benchmark. On a 10D correlated RBM benchmark, HCN achieves 3.829% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8 against a simulation reference, compared with 19.386% for an independent-marginal baseline.
item.dc:creator: Kehan Wang
